title: Phase 79 EFFECTIVELY-ONCE (eo) fault matrix - deployed Shuffle action task -> IRIS, create-only dedup/ledger

execution_provenance.note: Every matrix scenario ran inside the deployed Shuffle action task (execute_python node of workflow c6b3fcd8) reached through the live webhook trigger; the node emitted its own container/pid/netns/execution provenance. Host-side python was used only to POST the synthetic webhook events and to read back independent confirmations (IRIS Postgres count, ledger reads).

container_hosts_alignment.change: in shuffle-tools task .1 (f427c787867e) /etc/hosts, 'shuffle-opensearch' was repointed from the firewalled published address 172.20.0.1 to the reachable container address 172.20.0.3 (task .2 already had this entry)
container_hosts_alignment.reason: the host-published OpenSearch endpoint 172.20.0.1:9200 is firewalled from the execution sandbox (connect timeout), so the canonical v2 ledger claim could not be written from task .1; both tasks now reach the ledger over the cert-valid hostname with full TLS verification
container_hosts_alignment.scope: runtime-only, ephemeral (reverts on task recreate), no compose/service change

findings: Canonical v2 is fail-OPEN on ledger unavailability: a claim exception (cr = None) falls through to the destination POST, so an unreachable ledger yields a destination object with no ledger record (duplicate risk on retry). The matrix build used a fail-closed claim (LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE_FAIL_CLOSED, no POST). Recommended follow-up: adopt the fail-closed claim in the deployed node.

Ledger reachability from the execution sandbox depends on a container /etc/hosts entry rather than service discovery; it should be pinned in the service definition (extra_hosts or an overlay attachment) instead of a runtime edit.

One of 10 concurrent race executions (210df228) stalled in EXECUTING without recording the second action result; delivery correctness was unaffected (exactly one object) but Shuffle result-recording under burst is a durability observation.
dedup_writer is correctly least-privileged: 403 on indices:monitor/settings/get and indices:admin/aliases/get, 200 on document read/write.
limitations: crash_after_accept was simulated by aborting the action in-process after destination acceptance (restarting the shared shuffle-tools swarm task was out of scope for a non-disruptive run); the resulting ledger state (CLAIMED without alert_id) is identical to a real crash window.
partial_success simulated the ledger-finalize failure by directing the finalize write to an unreachable ledger port (real ConnectionError) rather than degrading the live OpenSearch service.
timeout_ambiguity required a 2 ms client read budget because the live destination answers in under 50 ms; the timeout, the abandoned response and the created object are all real.
Synthetic IRIS alerts 631-642 are retained (isolated by unique markers, no case/counter/scorecard impact) so the exactly-once evidence stays verifiable; no IRIS DB deletions were performed.
